jobs.description: About usAirbus ist Pionier einer nachhaltigen Luft- und Raumfahrt für eine sichere und vereinte Welt. Das Unternehmen arbeitet ständig an Innovationen für effiziente und technologisch fortschrittliche Lösungen in den Bereichen Luft- und Raumfahrt, Verteidigung sowie vernetzte Dienstleistungen. Airbus bietet moderne und treibstoffeffiziente Verkehrsflugzeuge sowie dazugehörige Dienstleistungen an. Airbus ist auch führend in Europa im Bereich Verteidigung und Sicherheit und eines der größten Raumfahrtunternehmen der Welt. Im Bereich Hubschrauber stellt Airbus die weltweit effizientesten Lösungen und Dienstleistungen für zivile und militärische Hubschrauber bereit.Job descriptionIn order to support our Data Processing team, Airbus Defence and Space is looking for anIntern in Payload Data Processing for space-borne Instruments (d/f/m)Are you looking for an internship and want to get to know the work of a Data Processing Engineer (d/f/m) ?  Then apply now! We look forward to you supporting us in the Data Processing team as an intern (d/f/m)!- Location: Friedrichshafen- Start: march 2026- Duration: 3-6 monthsIn strong collaboration with the instrument engineering teams, the department develops the on-ground processing of scientific instrument measurement data.This internship deals with remote sensing data processing and software development (mixed scientific and engineering task) for Earth Observation missions. As an intern (d/f/m) you will learn about engineering in a cross-disciplinary and international team, Earth observation from space and space science methods, software development in a mixed science and industry context, professional software development (algorithm development and test, code hygiene, performance optimization, testing tool-chain, build chains).Your locationAt the Airbus site in Friedrichshafen you will be working on innovation where others spend their holidays. Enjoy panoramic views of Lake Constance while having lunch in our canteen. And after work, join one of our many corporate sports groups to go running, sailing or skiing.Your benefits- Attractive salary and work-life balance with a 35-hour week (flexitime).- A final thesis is possible after consultation with the department.- International environment with the opportunity to network globally.- Work with modern/diversified technologies.- At Airbus, we see you as a valuable team member and you are not hired to brew coffee, instead you are in close contact with the interfaces and are part of our weekly team meetings.- Opportunity to participate in the Generation Airbus Community to expand your own network.Your tasks and responsibilities- Understanding the Measurement Concept of the Earth Observation payload and its data processing concept.- Design, prototyping and analysis of algorithms for the geometric, radiometric and spectral processing of remote sensing data from space born instruments (imager, radar, sounder).- Ability to identify the activities of the development life cycle that are necessary to develop a system/product and provide the level of confidence which is consistent with regulation and program requirements.Desired skills and qualifications- Enrolled full-time student (d/f/m) within aerospace or numerical engineering, natural sciences, physics, mathematics, software engineering or similar field of study.- Basic experience in Matlab or Python.- Experience in the domain of Numerical Analysis/Computational Physics is an asset.- Experience in version control systems (e.g. git) and collaborative workflow is an asset.- German or English: fluent.Please upload the following documents: cover letter, CV, relevant transcripts, enrollment certificate.Not a 100% match? At Roche you can show up as yourself, embraced for the unique qualities you bring. Our culture encourages personal expression, open dialogue, and genuine connections,  where you are valued, accepted and respected for who you are, allowing you to thrive both personally and professionally. Join Roche, where every voice matters.The PositionAt Roche, you can be yourself and are valued for your uniqueness. Our corporate culture fosters personal development, open dialogue, and authentic connections. As a pioneer in healthcare, we know: Every minute counts. When a diagnostic system in a laboratory stands still, patients are waiting for vital results. You ensure that our systems run smoothly, thus contributing directly to securing the healthcare of tomorrow. Become part of Roche, where every voice matters.Your new team:You will be part of our EMEA Customer Support Center Hub here in Mannheim. We are a team of technical and application experts supporting customers in the RCSC countries (Germany, Austria, Switzerland, the Netherlands, Belgium, Greece, and Turkey). Cohesion and working in intercultural teams are important to us; we work closely networked, including with 2nd-level support and our colleagues in the field.Responsibilities | What awaits youAs a Technical Specialist (m/f/d), you are the technical interface to our customers and colleagues. Your goal is to find fast and sustainable solutions for complex inquiries. Your main tasks include:* As the central point of contact, you process customer and employee inquiries by phone and email.* You use remote services for customer support and, if necessary, simulate customer situations in our laboratory to quickly identify and resolve errors.* You document your solution approaches structured in our CRM system and handle advanced complaint management for medium-complexity issues.* You work closely with 2nd-level support and escalate product quality problems to the next competence level. Occasionally, you also support the technical field service during on-site activities.* We are flexible regarding your work location. Your place of work can be Mannheim (Germany), Almere (Netherlands) or Diegem (Belgium). In any case, you actively seek exchange and collaboration with your colleagues at the RCSC in Mannheim.Qualifications | What you bringIn addition to successfully completed training as a Medical Technical Assistant (MTA), Technician (e.g., Mechatronics, Medical Technology, Electrical Engineering), or a Bachelor's degree (e.g., Natural Sciences, IT, Chemical or Electrical Engineering), you have initial professional experience in the medical technology field, either through technical customer support (field service or hotline) or in a laboratory function. Furthermore, the following points round out your profile:* You speak fluent Dutch/Flemish (C1). You also communicate confidently in English (min. B1/B2). Fluent German speaking skills are desirable.* You have good user knowledge of medical analysis systems or, alternatively, know-how in robotics, mechanics, or electrical engineering. Basic IT network knowledge and familiarity with CRM tools are familiar to you.* You are strongly customer-oriented, a real team player in intercultural teams, and possess pronounced methodical competence in troubleshooting.Your Application We ask you for the following documents:* Current CVFurther documents are not mandatory at this time. Please note before submitting your application that no further documents can be added afterward.Apply now – we look forward to it!Your contact to us! With people. For people.Do you need further support?Please have a look at our FAQs, you will find them via https://careers.roche.com/global/en/faq.Who we areA healthier future drives us to innovate. Together, more than 100’000 employees across the globe are dedicated to advance science, ensuring everyone has access to healthcare today and for generations to come. Our efforts result in more than 26 million people treated with our medicines and over 30 billion tests conducted using our Diagnostics products. We empower each other to explore new possibilities, foster creativity, and keep our ambitions high, so we can deliver life-changing healthcare solutions that make a global impact.Let’s build a healthier future, together.Roche is an Equal Opportunity Employer.

jobs.description: MEAG, the asset manager of Munich Re and ERGO, contributes significantly to the success of the Munich Re Group. Our employees combine unique know-how in all relevant asset classes and are the driving force behind our success as one of the top asset managers worldwide. As a team, we are unbeatable – we have impressively proven this even in times of Corona. MEAG – All Assets. One Team. We are looking to further strengthening our highly motivated Transaction Team in the Infrastructure Equity division. Dynamic capital markets meet a strong team spirit and a modern working environment in Munich Schwabing. The Infrastructure Equity portfolio reflects MEAG's expertise in all major infrastructure sectors in Europe and the USA. MEAG IE follows a long-term orientated buy & build investment strategy within four main investment themes: Energy Transition, Sustainable Transport, Digital Infrastructure and Essential Infrastructure. We acquire minorities, co-control and majorities in mid-market companies in line with our core/ core+ investment approach and strive to grow them throughout our ownership with an pro-active asset management approachWith your endurance, decision-making strength and performance orientation, you make a significant contribution to our team's success. You are keen to actively shape the future in the infrastructure equity sector and have several years of professional experience in the field of alternative investments on the equity side. You like to get to the bottom of things and appreciate the diverse and very demanding requirements for direct investments. You are spurred on by challenges and have a hands-on mentality. You have identified the enormous, worldwide need for infrastructure investments and the transformation towards carbon neutrality as a highly attractive field of activity in which you would like to get involved with outstanding commitment.Your responsibilities:- Screen, identify and evaluate suitable equity direct investment opportunities within the infrastructure sector, with a focus on energy transition, sustainable transport, digital and essential infrastructure- Conduct financial modelling, valuations, and due diligence to assess the viability of potential investment opportunities- As part of a dealteam, lead comprehensive due diligence workstreams, including commercial, technical, financial, tax, insurance and ESG, among other- Prepare and present investment committee materials and coordinate the investment process with internal stakeholders- Assist in structuring processes and negotiating transaction documents, working closely with senior investment managers, co-investors, and external advisors- Collaborate with the asset management team, particularly during the post-closing handover and throughout sell-side processes- Contribute to the further development of investment strategies and fundraising of infrastructure equity products for institutional clients- Stay informed on market trends and regulatory changes, proactively organizing regular catch-up and pipeline calls with key partners and external advisors to ensure timely insights and strategic alignmentYour profile:- Degree in economics, finance, engineering, or a related field (additional qualifications such as CFA or equivalent are a strong advantage)- At least 3 years of professional experience in the investment sector, preferably with an investment bank, infrastructure or private equity investor, consulting firm or audit company- Strong financial modelling and analytical skills, with experience in project finance and infrastructure M&A transactions- Proven ability to manage multiple workstreams and contribute to deal execution- Possession of an established network within the sector to source high-potential opportunities- Fluency in English is required; proficiency in an additional European language is a plus (German language skills or a willingness to learn German is highly valued)Do you have excellent analytical skills, business fluent English and enjoy working in a global organization in a targeted and solution-oriented manner? If you are also flexible and able to adapt to changing markets, you are our first choice!These benefits await you:- Flexibility: Mobile work (option to work from home a few days a week), 30 days of vacation- Asset Accumulation & Retirement Planning: Company pension system & employee savings plan- Development: Intensive professional & personal development (internal & external offerings), LinkedIn Learning access- Health: Comprehensive company doctor services, Urban Sports cooperation- Family: pme family service, childcare allowance, care assistance, cooperation with daycare centers, flexible working hours- Other: Daily free lunch in our cafeteria, Free hot drinks & water, "Deutschland Ticket Job" subsidy, Events, Underground parking garage with e-charging infrastructure & much more! *Please note that this list is based on current collective agreements. PhD position or Postdoctoral researcher (m/f/d): Effects of global livestock management on wildlife movementSenckenberg Society for Nature Research (SGN), headquartered in Frankfurt am Main, is seeking to fill the following position at the Senckenberg Biodiversity and Climate Research Centre (SBiK-F), starting as of 01 January2027:PhD position or Postdoctoral researcher (m/f/d):Effects of global livestock management on wildlife movementitel (m/f/d)(Part-Time)Location: Frankfurt am MainEmployment scope: PhD position (65%) / PostDoc (up to 60%)Type of contract: Temporary, limited to 4 years, until 31.12.20230Remuneration: Collective agreement of the state Hesse (TV-H) / E 13The Senckenberg Society for Nature Research is a member of the Leibniz Association and has been investigating the “Earth System” worldwide for more than 200 years, examining the past, analysing the present, and developing projections for the future. We conduct integrative geobiodiversity research with the aim of understanding nature in all its complexity and diversity in order to preserve it as the foundation of life for future generations and to ensure its sustainable use. Across eight institutes and five research stations throughout Germany, scientists from more than 40 countries conduct research at the highest international level.The mission of the Senckenberg Biodiversity and Climate Research Centre is to study the complex interactions between biodiversity, climate and society.As part of the Centre, the group “Global Land Systems and Biodiversity” takes a system perspective on how production, trade and consumption of food and other biomass products affect ecosystems and people.The VEBITA project, conducted jointly by SGN, the Marburg University and the Institute for Social-Ecological Research (ISOE) brings together researchers and practice partners to work towards utilizing animal movement data for early-warning systems for nature conservation. By analyzing GPS and sensor data from animals with statistical and AI-based methods, VEBITA aims to detect how animal behaviors change in response to land use, climate change, habitat loss, infrastructure development, and other environmental pressures.The adverstised position focuses on the effects of livestock management on wildlife movements contributes a use-case for state-of-the art animal movement data. Currently, livestock keeping has the largest spatial footprint of all land uses and the global biomass of mammalian livestock exceeds that of all remaining wild mammals by an order of magnitude. How and where livestock are kept greatly impacts the movements of the remaining wild mammals.In this context, we seek to develop a refined biodiversity footprint approach that captures how different livestock management strategies impact movement of wild mammals and how management can be adapted to achieve more sustainable outcomes. This subproject is part of VEBITA’s transdisciplinary focus, and the design of the novel footprint approach will consider perspectives of different relevant societal stakeholder groups such as livestock farmers, conservationists, and regulators. Results and insights of this work will also feed back to international science-policy debates on how conservation and human activities can be aligned in the future.Your tasks- Advance existing biodiversity footprint approaches in the context of livestock production and wildlife movement- Classify global livestock management systems- Analyze global patterns of how livestock keeping influences movements of wild mammals- Actively engage in exchange and cooperation within VEBITA’s inter- and transdisciplinary project team- Participate in project meetings and contribute to project reporting- Publish results in international journals in cooperation with the project teamYour profile- MSc degree (or equivalent) for application for a PhD position or PhD degree for application as postdoctoral researcher in a relevant field, e.g., sustainability science, physical geography, ecology or another relevant field- Programming skills (R, Python or similar), familiarity in working with heterogenous datasets and their analysis- Excellent English language skills- Interest in working in an inter- and transdisciplinary project- Interest in applied science at the science-policy interfaceDesirable skills- Experience with stakeholder interactionsWe offer- access to an international network of scientists, policymakers and research organizations- an attractive job within the inspired and dynamic working environment of an internationally recognized research institution- flexible working hours – mobile working options – employee ID card with free admission to Senckenberg museums – annual special payment – collectively agreed vacation entitlement – company pension planSenckenberg is committed to diversity. Senckenberg – Leibniz Institution for Biodiversity and Earth System Research (SGN), headquartered in Frankfurt am Main, is seeking to fill the following position at its Department of River Ecology and Conservation in Gelnhausen, starting as soon as possible2 Postdoctoral Researchers (ecologists) (m/f/d)(full-time / part-time)Location: GelnhausenEmployment scope: full-time / part-time options are availableType of contract: limited two years / an extension is be possibleRemuneration: Collective agreement of the state Hesse (TV-H) E 13Senckenberg is one of the world’s leading research institutions in the field of Biodiversity and Earth System Research, with eight research institutes and three natural history museums across Germany and scientists from over 40 nations. Our headquarter is located in the thriving commercial metropolis of Frankfurt in the heart of Germany, which also hosts one of our most famous facilities, the Senckenberg Natural History Museum. The location of the available position is in a Senckenberg institute about 40 kilometers east of Frankfurt in Gelnhausen, a historic town accessible via public transport (rail and bus).We are looking for enthusiastic ecologists with a background in broad-scale biodiversity change, community ecology, macroecology, metacommunities, and/or analysis of ecological time series.The two positions are embedded in one or more of the following projects:1. Synthesis Center on Freshwater Biodiversity Change in Europe The Synthesis Center brings together and supports a broad variety of researchers and practitioners investigating a broad variety of fundamental and applied ecological questions, with a particular focus on broad-scale and long-term biodiversity change, community ecology, freshwater ecology, time series analyses, multiple stressor impacts, and conservation (see doi.org/10.1038/s41586-023-06400-1 for an example). Data for > 30,000 freshwater biodiversity time series across 30 European countries have already been compiled from rivers and lakes, covering invertebrates, fish, macrophytes, diatoms, and benthic algae, in collaboration with a large pan-European network of > 200 researchers. Positions involved in this project are expected to pursue similar questions using the already available data.2. EU Horizon Europe project BEAGLE (started on 1st October 2026)BEAGLE (Biodiversity methods for advanced monitoring at large scales) is an EU-funded project using new technology to enhance biodiversity monitoring across terrestrial, freshwater, and marine environments. Specifically, the project uses sensors, environmental DNA (eDNA) and AI, as well as citizen science to collect large-scale and high-quality biodiversity data across a consortium of 17 partners. Positions involved in this project will focus on several tasks, including European-scale biodiversity data mobilization activities (e.g., tracking down datasets and preparing them for use), and the learning and deployment of field-based methods for data collection (e.g., Malaise traps).
